source._comment: ocon#151 PHASE D — DO NOT REMOVE apikey/secret/password/jwt/authenticationConfig from this schema descriptor. These five inline-secret fields MUST stay declared here even though the RemoveMigratedSourceSecretFields repair step deletes the first four from the LIVE schema per-instance. WHY: OpenRegister's Schema::hydrate() applies `properties` via setProperties() — a WHOLESALE REPLACE — so a version-bumping register import (ImportHandler::handleSchema -> updateFromArray, verified at OR origin/development) PRUNES any property ABSENT from this JSON, UNGATED by an instance's migration state. Removing a field here would therefore drop it fleet-wide on the next upgrade that bumps the source schema version, orphaning every un-migrated inline secret. Removal happens ONLY in the repair step, per-instance, gated on a verified-clean raw scan. Permanently deleting these four from this JSON is a FUTURE change, valid only once the whole fleet has converged (tracked in ocon#232, the ocon#151 follow-up). ocon#232 UPDATE — authenticationConfig: it is now established that authenticationConfig is VESTIGIAL (no code authenticates from it; AuthenticationRuntime moved to configuration.authentication.* in b6470597, 2024-11-19). It is therefore NOT migrated to a credentialRef — a minted ref would never be resolved by anything — but REMOVED. That removal is per-instance and human-gated behind `occ openconnector:authentication-config --remove-authentication-config`, and deliberately NOT part of any repair step: the four fields above were migrated (their values survive in the broker) so an unattended on-upgrade drop loses nothing, whereas clearing authenticationConfig DELETES the only copy and must require human intent every time. authenticationConfig MUST STAY DECLARED HERE for exactly the same setProperties() prune reason as the four — an instance that never opted in must not have the property pruned from under it by a version-bumping import.

type.description: Source kind dispatched at runtime by CallService. Recognised types: 'api' (default HTTP), 'database' (DB query), 'file' (filesystem), 'soap' (SOAPService dispatch), 'dso' (Digitaal Stelsel Omgevingswet outbound status/besluit. Log/sandbox or generic REST, dispatched directly by DsoIngestService via the DsoConnectorProviderInterface seam. Not via CallService; inbound Verzoek receipt is a signed webhook, DSOController::receiveRequest(), independent of this source's configuration), 'peppol' (Peppol Access Point, dispatched directly by PeppolTransmissionService. Not via CallService), 'psd2' (PSD2 AIS aggregator, dispatched directly by BankfeedSyncService. Not via CallService), 'sms' (SMS channel. NotifyNL or sandbox, dispatched directly by SmsDispatchService. Not via CallService), 'payment' (live payment provider. Log/sandbox or Mollie. Dispatched directly by PaymentIntentService, not via CallService), 'kiss' (KISS / VNG Klantinteracties API. Log/sandbox or generic REST, dispatched directly by KissSyncService. Not via CallService), 'open-formulieren' (Open Formulieren inbound webhook signature config, verified directly by OpenFormulierenController::inbound(). Not via CallService), 'iwmo-ijw' (iWMO/iJW StUF iStandaarden Wmo/Jeugdwet bridge. Log/sandbox or generic REST, dispatched directly by IwmoIjwSyncService. Not via CallService), 'fsc' (FSC / Federatieve Service Connectiviteit directory + call routing. Log/sandbox or generic REST, dispatched directly by FscCallService. Not via CallService). Free-form to keep custom adapter types unblocked; CallService falls back to HTTP for unrecognised values.

configuration.description: Free-form structured config (provider-specific). `configuration.authentication` MAY carry a `credentialRef` object: `{"credentialId": "<uuid>"}` (primary) or `{"credentialName": "<name>"}` (convenience). To dispatch this source's calls in-process through the OpenRegister credential broker instead of embedding secrets. When `credentialRef` is present: any sibling field under `authentication` is a hard 409 config error at call time (embedded secrets are FORBIDDEN, never merged); setting both `credentialId` and `credentialName`, or an empty value, is a 409; an ambiguous `credentialName` (0 or >1 owned matches) is a 409; SOAP sources, asynchronous dispatch, and `cert`/`ssl_key` config are rejected in v1. The provider catalogue's host-lock is the sole authority for the target host. `location` remains configuration documentation. `configuration.decompress: "gzip"` hints that the fetched body is a gzip-compressed file (also auto-detected from a `.gz`-suffixed endpoint or an `application/gzip` response Content-Type). Gunzipped before the existing JSON/XML/JSONL parse attempts; `.tar.gz`/`.tar` archives are detected but NOT supported (logged + skipped). `configuration.listMethod`/`configuration.body` (pre-existing, see decideMethod/mergeSourceConfiguration) let a source declare a static POST body template. See `sourceConfig.paginationIn` below for advancing it across pages (change post-body-pagination).
configuration.title: Configuration

authentication.title: Authentication
authentication.description: The source's outbound authentication block. Two brokered shapes are recognised, and they never collide: (1) PROXY. `authentication.credentialRef` at the top level, which dispatches the whole call through OpenRegister's credential broker (BrokeredCallService::hasCredentialRef); any sibling key under `authentication` is then a hard 409 (BrokeredCallService::validateCredentialRef). (2) APP-SIDE INJECTION. Any leaf under `authentication` may itself be `{"credentialRef": {...}}`, whose sole key MUST be `credentialRef` (BrokeredCallService::isPlaceholder); the secret is resolved from Doriath and substituted in place at call time. Undeclared keys remain allowed: this block is deliberately open so every pre-existing auth mechanism keeps validating.

credentialRef.title: Credential Reference
credentialRef.description: A reference to a credential held by OpenRegister's broker, so the secret is never stored on this source. EXACTLY ONE of `credentialId` (primary) or `credentialName` (convenience): setting both, neither, an empty/non-string value, or any other key is a hard 409 config error at call time (BrokeredCallService::validateInnerRef + extractSingleRefValue). A `credentialName` resolving to 0 or >1 owned credentials is likewise a 409.

credentialId.title: Credential ID
credentialId.description: UUID of the broker credential to use. The primary, unambiguous form. The credential itself lives in OpenRegister's credential broker, NOT in this register: openconnector never holds the secret, only this identifier. `x-external-register` records that the target is owned by another app, which is why there is no `$ref`: OpenRegister resolves `$ref` within one register set and cannot reach another app's schema.

credentialName.title: Credential Name
credentialName.description: Name of the broker credential to use. Convenience form; resolved to a credentialId at call time and a 409 when it is ambiguous (0 or >1 owned matches).

consumer.description: A Consumer is an event-bus subscriber (webhook target, AMQP queue, etc.). Paired with EventSubscription (filter) and EventMessage (delivery record). See local ADR-013 for the event-bus model.

domains.description: Allowed source domains as hostname patterns: exact (api.example.com) or suffix wildcard (*.example.com, which also matches the apex example.com). Matched against the forward-confirmed reverse DNS (FCrDNS) of the caller's IP: never against Origin/Referer/Host, which callers control and can spoof. A source with no confirmed matching hostname is rejected with HTTP 403. Absent = unrestricted; an empty list matches nothing and therefore rejects every request. Combined with 'ips' as a union: the caller is allowed if it matches an entry in either list.
domains.title: Allowed Domains

ips.description: Allowed source IP addresses: exact IPv4/IPv6 (203.0.113.4, 2001:db8::1) or CIDR ranges (10.0.0.0/8, 2001:db8::/32). Matched against the client IP as Nextcloud derives it, which honours a forwarded header only from a proxy listed in the instance's trusted_proxies config: behind an untrusted-proxy setup this is the proxy's own address, so list that. A caller outside the list is rejected with HTTP 403. Absent = unrestricted; an empty list matches nothing and therefore rejects every request. Combined with 'domains' as a union: the caller is allowed if it matches an entry in either list.

sourceConfig.description: Source-specific configuration overrides. Notable recognised keys: `resultsPosition` (dot-path to the objects array in the response, or `_root`/`_object`); `format: "jsonl"`. The fetched (and, if gzip, decompressed) body is parsed as line-delimited JSON, one record per line, instead of whole-document JSON/XML. Pair with `resultsPosition: "_root"` since the parsed line array IS the records list; `paginationQuery` (field name/dot-path to bump per page, default `page`); `paginationIn: "body"` (default `"query"`). Substitutes the next page value into the source's static `configuration.body` JSON template at the `paginationQuery` dot-path instead of the query string, for POST-body sources (e.g. TED's v3 search) whose pagination cursor lives in the request body. `deletionRatioThreshold` (float 0.0-1.0, default 0.10). The maximum share of this synchronization's existing contracts that one cleanup pass may garbage-collect before the deletion-ratio guard aborts the pass (warning logged + SynchronizationDeletionGuardedEvent dispatched); override per synchronization for legitimately volatile sources, or supply the explicit `forceDeletion` run parameter for a one-off override. `cursorField` (dot-path to the comparable cursor value on a fetched record, e.g. `updatedAt`. Same dotted-path-lookup-with-throw convention as `idPosition`/`getOriginId`) and `cursorComparator` (`gt`|`gte`, informational. The engine always takes the maximum observed value). Read only when the synchronization's top-level `syncMode` is `incremental`, to compute the persisted `cursorWatermark` after each complete fetch.

syncMode.description: Fetch strategy for an extern→intern run. `full` (default, unchanged behavior) fetches the entire source result set every run and hash-diffs it against stored SynchronizationContracts, including garbage-collecting target objects no longer present in the source (`deleteInvalidObjects`). `incremental` injects the stored `cursorWatermark` into the source request (via `{{ cursor }}` Twig templating on `sourceConfig.endpoint`/`sourceConfig.query`) so only records changed since the watermark are fetched, advances the watermark only after a complete, successful fetch, and NEVER runs `deleteInvalidObjects`: an incremental fetch is a filtered subset of the source, so a target's absence from one run is not evidence of source deletion. An absent value is treated as `full`. No migration needed for existing Synchronizations.

cursorWatermark.description: Stored high-watermark cursor for `syncMode: incremental` (e.g. An ISO-8601 timestamp or a monotonically comparable id/token from `sourceConfig.cursorField`). Advances only after a complete, successful, non-test incremental run; left unchanged after an incomplete/rate-limited fetch so the next run retries from the same value. Clear via `POST /api/synchronizations/{id}/reset-cursor` to force the next run back to an unfiltered (empty-cursor) fetch: this does NOT change `syncMode` or re-enable deletion.
